court: New York Supreme Court, General Term
holding_summary: Where a householder contracted to board and lodge a family for a year and the boarder abandoned the arrangement without cause, the boarding-keeper could sue immediately for breach rather than waiting out the term, recovering damages only to the date she gave up the house, measured as the profit she would have made had defendant performed, less profits earned by reletting the vacated rooms to other lodgers.

quotes.text: The defendant admits that he did make an agreement with the plaintiff to board and lodge with her for a space of time equal to one year from the 24th March, 1815, to the 24th March, 1816, at the rate of eighty-five dollars per week.
The plaintiff owed the duty to'defendant to let the rooms to other lodgers and thus relieve the defendant.
The utmost amount would be the profit the plaintiff would have made if the defendant had performed.

court: New York Supreme Court, General Term
holding_summary: The court held that statutory summary proceedings for non-payment of rent apply to a lessee of a fully furnished house let at a gross rent, because the furniture is a mere incident to the letting and the rent, in law, issues out of the land only; the injunction restraining the landlord's summary proceedings was therefore reversed.

quotes.text: The provisions of the Revised Statutes authorizing the dispossession of a tenant by summary proceedings, for non-payment of rent, are applicable to a lessee of a furnished house at a gross rent; the furniture in such a case is but an incident, and the rent issues out of the land only.
